sentences.text: Coram: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE RONGON MUKHOPADHYAY HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE PRADEEP KUMAR SRIVASTAVA

-------
For the Appellant : Mr. Vikram Sinha, Adv. For the State : Mrs. Priya Shrestha, Spl. P.P. (through VC) For the Informant : Mr. Shailesh Kumar Singh, Adv.

Heard Mr. Vikram Sinha, learned counsel for the appellant and learned Spl. P.P. assisted by Mr.
Shailesh Kumar Singh, learned counsel appearing for the informant.
2. This application has been preferred by the appellant for grant of bail to him during the pendency of this appeal.

3. The appellant has been convicted for the offences under Section 376(2)(n) of the Indian Penal Code and Section 6 of the P.O.C.S.O. Act and has been sentenced to undergo R.I. for 20 years along with fine of Rs.10,000/- for the offence under Section 6 of the P.O.C.S.O. Act.

4. It has been alleged that the daughter of the informant was enticed by the appellant and she was subjected to sexual exploitation and it has further been alleged that some obscene photos and videos were also prepared and made viral by him.
5. Submission has been advanced by learned counsel for the appellant that though it has been Krishna Jeevan Pandey vs The State Of Jharkhand on 25 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79228866/
1 concluded by the learned Trial Court that the victim is a minor based on an admission register but the said admission register has not been properly proved by the prosecution.

entities.text: Krishna Jeevan Pandey vs The State Of Jharkhand
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Referring to the evidence of the doctor, it has been submitted that the age of the victim has been assessed to be 18-19 years.

Learned counsel while referring to the evidence of the victim, who has been examined as P.W.1, has stated that there was a love affair between the victim and the appellant and in fact the family members had wanted the victim to solemnize marriage with the appellant.
6. Learned Spl. P.P. as well as learned counsel appearing for the informant have opposed the prayer for bail of the appellant.
7. It appears from the evidence of P.W.1 that she was sexually exploited for a continuously long period of time and the Instagram/WhatsApp accounts do corroborate the said fact.

The victim has been found to be a minor based on entry made in the admission register and in such circumstances,
therefore, we are not inclined to admit the appellant on bail.
His prayer for bail is hereby rejected at this stage.
8. Accordingly, I.A. No.606 of 2026 stands rejected.

Dated: 25th February, 2026 Sachin/
